import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        ])
        
        # Colors
        color_parabola = "#1E90FF"
        color_ball = "#FF4500"
        color_error = "#FF4500"

        # Assets

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2.2, 2.2, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE},
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4
        )
        
        weight_label = Text("Weight", font_size=18, color=color_weight)
        error_label = Text("Error", font_size=18, color=color_error)
        
        parabola = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[-2, 2], color=color_parabola)
        
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, parabola)
        # Resolved Issue 35 & 36: Adjusted area and scale to prevent overlap with title and edge
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Position labels relative to axes after placement
        error_label.next_to(axes.y_axis, UP, buff=0.2)
        weight_label.next_to(axes.x_axis, RIGHT, buff=0.2)

        self.play(Create(axes), Write(error_label), Write(weight_label))
        self.play(Create(parabola))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualize this as a valley with a bottom.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        ball_start_x = 1.6
        ball_pos = axes.c2p(ball_start_x, ball_start_x**2)
        
        # Resolved Issue 28: Using provided SVG asset for the ball
        ball = SVGMobject(ball_asset)
        ball.set_color(color_ball)
        ball.scale(0.15) # Adjusted for visual balance
        ball.move_to(ball_pos)
        
        # Vertical distance line representing error
        dist_line = Line(
            start=axes.c2p(ball_start_x, 0),
            end=ball_pos,
            color=color_error,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        dist_text = Text("Gap", font_size=16, color=color_error).next_to(dist_line, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(FadeIn(ball), Create(dist_line), Write(dist_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The lowest point represents zero error and perfection.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Value tracker for rolling down the slope
        t = ValueTracker(ball_start_x)
        
        # Persistent updaters for smooth motion
        ball.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(t.get_value(), t.get_value()**2)))
        dist_line.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners([
            axes.c2p(t.get_value(), 0),
            axes.c2p(t.get_value(), t.get_value()**2)
        ]))
        dist_text.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dist_line, LEFT, buff=0.1))

        # Roll the ball to the bottom
        self.play(
            t.animate.set_value(0),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        
        # Final highlight at the zero-error point
        ball.clear_updaters()
        dist_line.clear_updaters()
        dist_text.clear_updaters()
        
        self.play(
            ball.animate.scale(1.5).set_color(GOLD),
            FadeOut(dist_line),
            FadeOut(dist_text)
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

        title = "Intuitive Backpropagation: The Blame Game"
        lines = [
            "Backpropagation identifies which weights caused the error.",
            "We work backward from the output to input.",
            "Think of tracing blame through a relay race.",
            "The final error tells us what to change.",
            "We distribute adjustments based on individual contributions."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Assets
        GEAR_ASSET = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/gears.svg"
        RELAY_ASSET = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/relay.svg"

        # Initialize velocity tracker for updaters
        self.gear_vel = ValueTracker(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show three connected gray gears ([Asset: gears.svg]) spinning; 
        # final gear reaches a red 'Error' marker (#FF0000).
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#A9A9A9")
        
        gear1 = SVGMobject(GEAR_ASSET).set_color("#A9A9A9")
        gear2 = SVGMobject(GEAR_ASSET).set_color("#A9A9A9")
        gear3 = SVGMobject(GEAR_ASSET).set_color("#A9A9A9")

        # Issue 37: Reposition gears to 'C4', 'C5', 'C6', with scale_factor 0.7
        self.place_at_grid(gear1, "C4", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(gear2, "C5", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(gear3, "C6", scale_factor=0.7)

        # Add persistent rotation updaters
        gear1.add_updater(lambda g, dt: g.rotate(self.gear_vel.get_value() * dt))
        gear2.add_updater(lambda g, dt: g.rotate(-self.gear_vel.get_value() * dt))
        gear3.add_updater(lambda g, dt: g.rotate(self.gear_vel.get_value() * dt))

        self.add(gear1, gear2, gear3)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # We work backward from the output to input.
        # A red 'Blame' pulse (#FF0000) travels backward from output gear to input gear.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")

        # Issue 38: error_marker 'D6', error_label 'D5', scale_factor 0.8

        error_label = Text("Error", color="#FF0000", font_size=16)
        self.place_at_grid(error_label, "D5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.place_at_grid(blame_pulse, "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.add(blame_pulse)
        self.play(
            blame_pulse.animate.move_to(self.grid["C4"]).set_stroke(width=10).scale(1.5),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(blame_pulse))
        self.wait(1)

            # x=0, y=0.5*x**2 maps to center + (0, -1.5625)

outline.topic: Neural Network Learning and Intuitive Backpropagation
outline.target_audience: University students and beginning AI enthusiasts

sections.title: The Big Picture: Learning as Trial and Error
sections.content: Introduce the goal of a neural network: to minimize the difference between its guess and the actual truth. Explain that 'learning' is just the process of adjusting internal knobs (weights) to get a better result.
sections.example: Imagine a robot archer trying to hit a bullseye. At first, it's terrible. Learning is the process of the robot observing how far it missed and adjusting its arm tension for the next shot.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Weighted Connection
sections.content: Before diving into learning, visualize a single neuron. An input comes in, gets multiplied by a 'Weight' (significance), and produces an output. Use a graphical slider to represent the weight.
sections.example: Think of a 'Cooking AI'. Input: Amount of Salt. Weight: Importance of salt for taste. Output: Flavor Score. If the weight is high, a small change in salt drastically changes the flavor.

sections.title: The Error (Loss) Function
sections.content: Define 'Error' as the gap between the predicted output and the target. Mathematically, visualize this as a 'U-shaped' valley (a parabola) where the bottom of the valley represents zero error.
sections.example: A thermometer says it's 25°C, but the real temperature is 20°C. The 'Error' is 5 units. Our goal is to roll a ball down to the bottom of the temperature-error valley.

sections.title: Intuitive Backpropagation: The Blame Game
sections.content: Introduce Backpropagation as 'working backwards' from the error to find out which weight caused the mistake. Visualize a chain of gears: if the last gear turns too far, we trace back to see how much each previous gear contributed.
sections.example: In a relay race, if the team loses, the coach looks at the finish line (error) and walks backward to the previous runners to see who was lagging the most. That person gets the most 'blame' (adjustment).

sections.title: The Chain Rule: A Ripple Effect
sections.content: Explain the math of Backpropagation using the Chain Rule, but visualize it as a 'Sensitivity Analysis'. If I change Weight A by a tiny bit, how much does the Error change? This is the Gradient (Slope).
sections.example: Animation: A small nudge to a domino at the start of a line. We calculate how that nudge ripples through the network to finally move the 'Error' domino at the end.

sections.title: Gradient Descent: Taking the Step
sections.content: Once we know the 'direction' of the error (the gradient), we update the weights in the opposite direction. Introduce the 'Learning Rate' as the size of the step we take down the hill.
sections.example: A blindfolded hiker (the algorithm) feeling the slope of a mountain with their feet. If the slope goes up to the right, they take a small step to the left to find the valley floor.

sections.title: The Result: Convergence
sections.content: Summarize how repeating this process (Forward pass -> Calculate Error -> Backpropagate -> Update Weights) eventually leads to a smart network.
sections.example: Show the robot archer from Section 1. After 100 rounds of backpropagation, its 'arm tension' weights are perfect, and it hits the bullseye every single time.

storyboard.title: The Big Picture: Learning as Trial and Error
lecture_lines: Neural networks learn through simple trial and error.
The goal is to minimize prediction errors.
Adjusting internal weights brings us closer to truth.
animations: Robot [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] archer [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/archer.svg] (#FFD700) aims at bullseye (#FF4500) and misses, showing high prediction error (#FF0000).
Highlight the distance between arrow and center; adjust 'Arm Tension' (#00FF00) slider weights.
Robot [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] shoots again and hits the bullseye center (#FF4500).

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Weighted Connection
lecture_lines: Neurons process inputs through weighted connections.
Weights determine the significance of each input.
Adjusting these weights changes the final output signal.
animations: Neuron circle (#00FFFF) processes 'Salt' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/salt.svg] input through a connection with a yellow weight (#FFFF00).
Show 'Flavor Score' (#FF00FF) impact, highlighting the weight significance on the connection line.
Moving the Weight slider (#FFFF00) changes the final Flavor Score output signal.

storyboard.title: The Error (Loss) Function
lecture_lines: The loss function measures our distance from success.
Visualize this as a valley with a bottom.
The lowest point represents zero error and perfection.
animations: Draw a blue U-shaped loss function (#1E90FF) showing vertical distance from success.
Place the ball [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg] on the slope representing the current error level (#FF4500).
The ball [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg] rolls to the bottom of the parabola, reaching the zero-error point.

storyboard.title: Intuitive Backpropagation: The Blame Game
lecture_lines: Backpropagation identifies which weights caused the error.
We work backward from the output to input.
Think of tracing blame through a relay race.
The final error tells us what to change.
We distribute adjustments based on individual contributions.
animations: Show three connected gray gears ([Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/gears.svg]) spinning; final gear reaches a red 'Error' marker (#FF0000).
A red 'Blame' pulse (#FF0000) travels backward from output gear to input gear.
A relay race icon ([Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/relay.svg]) traces the blame path through the gears.
Display the final error value (#FF0000) indicating the necessary total change.
Gears ([Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/gears.svg]) glow red (#FF0000) proportionally to their contribution and adjust rotation speed.

storyboard.title: The Chain Rule: A Ripple Effect
lecture_lines: The chain rule calculates the ripple of error.
It measures weight sensitivity through the network.
A small nudge at the start affects everything.
Gradients tell us the direction of steepest slope.
We follow these slopes to reduce overall error.
animations: Align a row of white dominos (#FFFFFF) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/domino.svg]; a 'Total Error' box (#FF4500) sits at the end.
A yellow arrow (#FFD700) nudges the first domino [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/domino.svg], measuring weight sensitivity.
A cyan wave (#00FFFF) ripples through all dominos [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/domino.svg], demonstrating the Chain Rule.
Green gradient arrows (#00FF00) appear on each domino [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/domino.svg] showing the direction of steepest slope.
The 'Total Error' box shifts position as dominos [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/domino.svg] fall, reducing overall error.

storyboard.title: Gradient Descent: Taking the Step
lecture_lines: Gradient descent moves us down the error hill.
We update weights in the downhill direction.
The learning rate controls our step size.
Careful steps prevent overshooting the valley floor.
Gradually, we converge on the lowest possible error.
animations: A hiker [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hiker.svg] (#FFD700) stands on a brown error hill (#8B4513).
The hiker [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hiker.svg] observes a green gradient arrow (#00FF00) pointing downhill.
The hiker [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hiker.svg] takes a step; a 'Learning Rate' slider (#FFFF00) controls the step size.
The hiker [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hiker.svg] takes careful steps downward, avoiding overshooting the valley floor.
The hiker [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hiker.svg] converges at the lowest point of the valley with minimal error.

storyboard.title: The Result: Convergence
lecture_lines: Repeating this cycle creates an intelligent network.
After many rounds, the robot hits the bullseye.
The system has learned the optimal internal weights.
animations: [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] archer (#FFD700) rapidly repeats the cycle: Forward Pass, Error, Backprop, Update.
After many training rounds, the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg]'s arrow hits the bullseye (#FF4500) perfectly.
Weight knobs (#00FF00) lock in place as the system achieves convergence.
